questions.heading: A Tied Model Has Many Optimal Plans, and "Optimal" Is a Range
questions.stem: Two runs of one maximization MIP, with different seeds and default settings, both report OPTIMAL, with objectives 512,040 and 512,071. What does that tell you?

options.text: One run is wrong, since an OPTIMAL plan of 512,040 is beaten by 512,071
options.says: OPTIMAL means within the gap of the bound; 31 is under 0.01% of 512,071, so both count.

options.text: Both can count as optimal, since 31 is under 0.01% of about 512,000
options.says: Right: the page's Gurobi runs reported four OPTIMAL objectives within 0.01% of each other.

options.text: The seeds moved the true optimum, by 31, between the two runs
options.says: A seed changes the path, not the model; the page says a gap tolerance lets different plans count as optimal.

options.text: A time limit stopped one run, 31 short of the plan the other found
options.says: A run stopped by a time limit reports FEASIBLE on the page, not OPTIMAL.

questions.heading: One Solve With an ε Weight Works Only Between Two Bounds
questions.stem: A crew model maximizes crews hired + ε × (sum of crew ratings), with 50 candidate crews each rated 1 to 10. Below which value must ε stay so that the ratings can never trade a crew away?

options.text: ε below 1/501, since all 50 ratings together can add up to 500
options.says: Right: the page bounds ε by the largest total the second term can reach over a plan, here 50 × 10 = 500.

options.text: ε below 1/11, since a single crew's rating can add up to 10
options.says: The page's bound uses the largest total over a whole plan, not one crew's share: 500, not 10.

options.text: ε below 1/51, since the model can hire up to 50 crews in all
options.says: The bound comes from the second term, the ratings; the number of crews is the first term.

options.text: ε below 1e-4, since that is the solver's default relative gap
options.says: The page shows a weight that small falls under the solver's tolerances and is ignored.

questions.heading: Tie-Break Weights Must Repeat in Every Process and Separate the Plans
questions.stem: A team breaks ties with weights 1, 2, ..., n by sorted variable name and an ε small enough never to outweigh the main objective. What can still go wrong?

options.text: The weights can shift between processes, since sorted order follows the hash salt
options.says: sorted() depends only on the characters; the page's rank weights were the same in every process.

options.text: Two variables can share a weight, since two names can sort to the same rank
options.says: Rank weights are 1, 2, ..., n, one per variable; the page notes no two variables share a weight.

options.text: The weights can differ by build order, since rank follows the order added
options.says: The rank comes from sorted(keys), whatever order the code added them in.

options.text: Two plans can reach the same total weight, so the tie-break can tie as well
options.says: Right: rank weights repeated in every process yet left two plans with the same total, 1,281.
